sections.h2: What does the Northampton County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The office keeps the county's permanent real estate records: deeds, deeds of trust, plats, UCC filings and vital records. For a seller, the office matters because it files the deed that hands title to the buyer, along with any deed of trust the buyer's lender takes.

According to the county, the oldest land records go back to 1741. Marriage records begin in 1863, and birth and death records in December 1913. Older entries are located through paper indexes. The same staff issue marriage licenses and certified vital records, so say at the start of a call that you are asking about a deed.

The county office page gives 252-534-2511 for questions. Ask there for the street address, hours and holiday closings, which this guide does not list.

sections.h2: How do I search Northampton County land records online?
sections.html:
Land records from January 1, 1991 to the present are free to search at northamptonrod.org. The county says this was the first time the records appeared on the internet, and the computerized index covers only that range.

  • Search from 1991 forward on the website for deeds, deeds of trust and releases.
  • For older records, plan on the hard-copy indexes at the office.
  • Use the parcel owner's name as it appears on the last recorded deed, since indexes follow the names on the document.

A chain of title for a family farm or an inherited lot often starts before 1991. If your parcel passed through several generations, call the office before you assume the online index shows everything.

sections.h2: What does Northampton County's housing market look like?
sections.html:
Northampton is one of the state's thinly settled counties. Census Bureau data show 16,491 residents as of the July 2025 estimate, spread over 536.70 square miles of land, a drop of 5.6 percent since the April 2020 base and a long way under the 22,099 recorded in 2010. In 2020 there were 32.6 residents for each square mile.

Most homes here are lived in by their owners. Across 7,857 households (2020 to 2024 survey period), 74.6 percent own the place they live in. The median owned home is worth $114,500, and median gross rent is $758. Nearly a third of the population, 31.5 percent, is 65 or older. Builders pulled just 15 permits in 2025, and 91.9 percent of residents were in the same house one year earlier.

For a long-held house, a clean recorded chain of title matters most, and a gap in the index is easier to fix before a buyer's title search finds it. The figures above come from Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Northampton County?
sections.html:
North Carolina sets one fee schedule for every county, so Northampton collects the same amounts as its neighbors. The table reproduces the list kept by the state association of registers of deeds, last updated February 5, 2024.

Register of deeds fee list for real estate filings
FilingFee
Ordinary instrument, including a deed$26 covers 15 pages; $4 per extra page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 covers 35 pages; $4 per extra page
Plat$21 a sheet
Nonstandard document$25
Several instruments combined in one$10 for each
Satisfaction of a deed of trust or mortgageFree
Certified copy$5 for page one, $2 for each after

G.S. 161-10 backs the list and describes the fees as complete and exclusive, payable up front. The closing agent usually sends a check with the deed.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed tax in a Northampton County sale?
sections.html:
The seller does. North Carolina taxes each deed at $1 per $500 of consideration, counting any leftover under $500 as a full $500. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the transferor hands that payment to the register before the deed is filed. Half stays in the county general fund, and the other half goes to the state revenue department through a monthly remittance.

The county's office page also links a Deed Tax Certification form, a notice on deed of trust fee changes and a redaction request for public records. Ask which of these your closing requires.

sections.h2: What else does the office record that affects a sale?
sections.html:
Besides the deed, the office files the lender's deed of trust, releases and plats. A release costs nothing, since the fee list shows no charge for satisfactions, so a paid-off loan has no cost reason to stay open. A buyer's lender will want it cleared.

  • A plat is $21 a sheet, which applies if a lot is split before sale.
  • A nonstandard document adds $25.
  • An assignment with more index references costs $10 for each extra reference, and an indexed party past the twentieth adds $2 a name.
  • A UCC record runs $38 for one or two pages.

An owner with several parcels, or with an older estate property, can ask the office to check the index for liens, releases and prior deeds before the closing date. The online index begins in 1991, so earlier instruments mean a phone call.

sections.h2: What questions should I settle before I list a Northampton County house?
sections.html:
Three offices share the paperwork on a sale: the register of deeds, the tax department and the clerk of court if an estate is involved. A short checklist keeps them from tripping you up at closing.

  • Find the last recorded deed and confirm the names on it match the people signing.
  • Look for an unreleased deed of trust in the index from 1991 forward, and call the office about anything older.
  • Ask the tax department for the balance due on every year still open, and whether any county bill remains from earlier years.
  • Pull the parcel's property tax card and GIS map, which the tax page links, so the acreage and description match the deed.
  • If the owner has died, confirm with the clerk of court who has authority to sign and whether the will has been probated.

The tax page also links a room occupancy tax return, so anyone who ran lodging at the property should ask the tax department how to close out that account.

sections.h2: What should I send to the office to record a deed?
sections.html:
Send the signed deed with payment and a self-addressed, stamped return envelope, which the county asks for with every filing.

  • Compare the deed with the recording standards on the North Carolina Association of Registers of Deeds website.
  • Include payment for the filing fee and the seller's deed tax.
  • Phone the office to learn whether it accepts mail, courier packages or drop-off.
  • Keep your recording confirmation. Under G.S. 47-18 a deed gains effect against creditors and later buyers only once it is registered.

Filings rank by time of registration, so a deed that arrives late can fall behind a lien that was recorded first.

sections.h2: Which other county office matters before you sell?
sections.html:
Tax bills for a Northampton parcel come from the Northampton County Tax Department at 126 E. Jefferson St. in Jackson. Its page gives September 1, 2026 as the due date for 2026 bills and says interest does not begin until after January 5, 2027. Numbers listed there: 252-534-4461 for the main office, 252-534-5941 for land records and 252-534-3431 for listing.

The tax page links appeal forms and a list of county property for sale. Before choosing a closing date, ask the tax office what balance would clear the parcel. If you would rather skip repairs and showings on a Northampton County house, Cash Home Buyers can send a cash offer to weigh against your payoff and recording costs.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for Northampton County property?
faqs.a: The Northampton County Register of Deeds records it. A deed takes effect against creditors and later buyers once registered in the county where the parcel lies, per G.S. 47-18. Phone 252-534-2511 for the street address and hours.

faqs.q: How much is a deed filing fee in Northampton County?
faqs.a: A deed runs $26 for the first 15 pages with $4 added per extra page, and a deed of trust $64 for 35 pages with the same $4 add-on. The seller's deed tax, $1 per $500 of price, is a separate payment.

faqs.q: Can I search Northampton County land records for free?
faqs.a: Yes, from 1991 forward. The county says land records from January 1, 1991 to the present are free at northamptonrod.org, while older records are searched in paper indexes at the office.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax when a Northampton County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the payment on the transferor, due at the register of deeds before filing, at $1 per $500 of consideration.

faqs.q: When are Northampton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. The Tax Department says interest on 2026 bills starts only after January 5, 2027. State law then adds 2 percent through January and 0.75 percent per month afterward.
